messages:
Anne: Hey team — prepping the webinar/launch post. Need a quick variance sanity check on the benchmark numbers we quoted. Can the runtime folks confirm methodology and rerun with minimal noise?
Ravi: @Anne can you scope: which model variants, configs, and top-line metrics you need? p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost?
Anne: Yes — p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), and cost per 1k tokens. Compare: FP16 baseline vs 8-bit quantized vs 4-bit quantized. Also please include batch sizes 1, 8, 32.
Chris: We should also surface variance across prompt styles. I can provide a 200-sample prompt set: short, long, and instruction-style.
Anne: That would be great. Prioritize the short+instruction hybrid for the webinar demo.
Maria: Got it. We'll run the three quantization configs across the three batches with the 200-sample set. Any target SLOs?
Sam: For marketing, we care if p95 > 300ms or cost delta > 2x relative to FP16. Callouts on anything outside that.
Ravi: Two quick asks from runtime side: (1) which seed/ determinism to use? (2) include warmed vs cold-run? Cold runs skew p50/p95.
Anne: Use seed=42 for reproducibility. Include both warmed (run a single warmup pass) and cold (first-run) numbers, but mark them separately in the table.
Maria: OK. Draft run command I'll use: 
```bash
./run_bench 
  --model redwood-13b 
  --variant {fp16,8bit,4bit} 
  --batch-size {1,8,32} 
  --seq-len 512 
  --seed 42 
  --samples 200 
  --warmup 1
  --output results/{variant}_b{batch}.csv
```
Ravi: Perfect. Also capture p50/p95/p99 latency per-token and per-request, plus tokens/s. Export CSV with columns: variant,batch,seed,warmup,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1k.
Chris: I can run a quick sanity script after results land to compute confidence intervals and flag anomalies.
Maria: Starting the runs now. Will push artifacts to the shared bucket and paste links. Expect ~45 minutes.
bench-bot: bench job queued — job_id=bench-1934567800-01, ETA ~40m
Ravi: Thanks — when results land, please include raw logs for any p95 outliers. We'll try to correlate with GC/distro events.
Anne: If anything looks off, we may ask for a small rerun with seq-len 1024 for the long-prompt check.
Maria: Noted. Kicking off. I'll ping here with the S3 link once uploaded.
Chris: Thanks folks — will prep the slide snippet template so marketing can drop the numbers in once validated.
Anne: Awesome. Appreciate the quick turn. :pray: If the numbers stay within bounds I'll draft the benchmark blurb and share for legal review.
Maria: upload complete: s3://redwood-bench/marketing/1934567800/results.tar.gz — contains CSVs + logs + run_metadata.json
Ravi: Downloaded and skimmed. Quick note: 4-bit runs show higher variance at batch=32, p95 spikes on two samples — tagging those rows.
Chris: Running the anomaly script now. If it's only 2/200 samples we can annotate as corner cases in the notes.
Maria: Anomaly script output: 2 samples flagged (both long prompts), p95 increased ~1.8x vs fp16 at batch=32 in 4-bit. Warmed runs for batch<=8 look stable.
Anne: Good to know. Can we get a tiny rerun for those 2 prompts with seq-len 1024 and batch 8 confirm?
Ravi: Will do a focused rerun. Reusing same seed.
bench-bot: rerun job queued — job_id=bench-1934567800-02, ETA ~6m
Maria: Focused rerun finished: s3://redwood-bench/marketing/1934567800/rerun_2prompts.tar.gz — results show similar overhead at seq=1024 but p95 reduced when we drop to batch=8.
Ravi: Conclusion: 4-bit quantized variant is fine for most marketing claims if we note the edge-case caveat (long prompts + large batch -> p95 increase). Recommend we list numbers for batch=1 and 8 in the public table and call out caution for batch>=32.
Anne: Perfect. That's the nuance we needed. Can someone paste the summarized table (CSV -> 3 row summary per variant) here for me to copy into the blog?
Chris: Pasted summary: 
FP16, batch=1, p95=85ms, tokens/s=520, cost_per_1k=$0.12
FP16, batch=8, p95=92ms, tokens/s=410, cost_per_1k=$0.09
8bit, batch=1, p95=95ms, tokens/s=560, cost_per_1k=$0.08
8bit, batch=8, p95=110ms, tokens/s=450, cost_per_1k=$0.06
4bit, batch=1, p95=120ms, tokens/s=730, cost_per_1k=$0.05
4bit, batch=8, p95=210ms, tokens/s=680, cost_per_1k=$0.04
(see attached CSVs for p50/p99 and warmed/cold splits)
Anne: This is gold. Adding the caveat about long-prompt/batch>=32 causing p95 spikes. Thanks everyone!
Ravi: Adding a short note to runtime docs about recommended batch caps for 4-bit quantization and a pointer to this thread.
Maria: Done — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-docs/pull/412
Anne: Linking the PR in the marketing doc and moving forward. :rocket:
